audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor predates the headquarters financing burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $99.181 million finance obligation at June 28, 2026 and $110.0 million of noncancellable lease payments; post-completion owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-completion interest and other economic financing costs would reduce equity-level owner earnings; any residual-value or purchase-option claim not captured through owner earnings may also affect the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: There will be no material impact to the statements of income until construction completion, which is expected in the latter half of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is prospective rather than an error in FY2025 earnings: the filing confirms no material income-statement effect before construction completion. The valuation does not separately forecast the burden beginning in the third quarter of 2026. The recorded obligation equals 1.6% of the $6,349 million base equity value, but principal should not be mechanically deducted under the stated equity-OE method. Interest, amortization economics and the undetermined residual guarantee are insufficiently quantified to establish whether the valuation effect is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the completed-project cost, building-versus-land allocation, effective interest schedule, annual cash payments, purchase-option terms and final residual-value guarantee; insert the resulting after-tax economic costs into forecast owner earnings and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Large signed leases have not yet entered reported rent expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,175.9 million of nominal uncommenced lease commitments, including $14.2 million in 2026 and $1,161.7 million thereafter; net value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Commencement adds rent, occupancy costs and opening drag to owner earnings while the associated new stores may add sales and operating profit; the net store economics determine achievable OE growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Real estate obligations, which include legally binding minimum lease payments for leases executed but not yet commenced, were $ 1,175.9 million as of December 28, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are filed and equal 18.5% of the $6,349 million base equity value, but they are not an equity claim to deduct mechanically. The record does not map the future rent to store openings, landlord allowances, ramp losses or mature-store contribution, so neither the net direction nor materiality of the forecast error is established.
audit_findings.action: Build a store-by-store commencement schedule from executed leases, including fixed and variable rent, tenant allowances, pre-opening costs, expected cannibalization and contribution margins; reconcile the resulting net owner earnings to each scenario and rerun if not already embedded.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require reinvestment not captured by simple OE growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $280 million-$310 million of filed 2026 capex; applying 3% and 6% growth to the $435.9 million anchor at 80.7% RONTA implies approximately $16.2 million and $32.4 million of first-year reinvestment, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth-related capital spending reduces distributable owner earnings; crediting OE growth without its required incremental investment inflates forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect capital expenditures to be in the range of $280 million to $310 million in 2026, net of estimated landlord tenant improvement allowances, primarily to fund investments in new stores, remodels, maintenance capital expenditures and corporate capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The planned capex equals 64%-71% of anchor owner earnings and is materially above 2025 cash capex of $248.267 million. The filing does not separate maintenance, expansion, remodel and corporate spending, but the computed reinvestment implied by the stated growth and RONTA is 3.7% of anchor OE in base and 7.4% in bull. That scale is reasonably capable of materially changing scenario values, particularly the bull value of $78.35 per share.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance from expansion capex and landlord reimbursements, reconcile both to the OE calculation, explicitly deduct the incremental investment required by each growth path at the stated RONTA, and rerun operating PV, terminal value, value per share and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: A quantified litigation claim is not represented in normalized earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: The final settlement payment and unreimbursed legal costs would be one-time reductions to equity value rather than recurring normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequently, on February 24, 2025, Harvest Sherwood filed a complaint against the Company in the Superior Court for the State of Delaware alleging breach of contract among other claims and seeking monetary damages of approximately $ 42.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q reports an agreement to settle all Harvest Sherwood claims and counterclaims for an amount described by the filer as immaterial, with court approval on July 27, 2026. Even the superseded $42.0 million gross claim would equal only 0.66% of the $6,349 million base equity value, or approximately $0.44 per diluted share, and the actual settlement is smaller. It therefore cannot reasonably change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm expiration of the appeal period and obtain the final payment and defense-cost amounts; record them as a one-time bridge adjustment only if the aggregate ceases to be immaterial.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 earnings contain tax benefits that may not recur
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.629 million identified 2025 tax benefit: $13.123 million from excess share-based-payment benefits plus $3.506 million from transferable-credit discounts; computed maximum valuation effect approximately $275.7 million or $2.90 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax benefits raise reported net income and historical OE, potentially raising the log-trend anchor and every scenario derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective income tax rate decreased to 24.0 % in 2025 from 24.9 % in 2024 primarily due to an increased benefit for stock-based compensation in the current year and benefit for purchase discount on tax credits partially offset by an increase in nondeductible officer compensation and the rate benefit in prior year due to receipt of interest related to the 2017 amended federal return refund.
audit_findings.explanation: The identified benefits equal 3.8% of the $435.9 million anchor. As a conservative bound, assuming the full $16.629 million entered the trend anchor dollar-for-dollar and applying the bull operating-PV multiple of 16.58 produces a $2.90-per-share effect. The actual trend effect must be smaller because only one observation is affected. Even this bound would reduce the already-below-market bull value from $78.35 to about $75.45 versus the $81.40 price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recompute the historical OE series after removing the $13.123 million excess award-tax benefit and $3.506 million transferable-credit discount while retaining SBC expense, refit the trend anchor, and document the resulting immaterial scenario changes.
